clue.text: A light sweet

blocks.note: first meaning: a lantern with a thick convex lens, as carried by old policemen
second meaning: a large round hard boiled sweet, often striped

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a dessert that is not heavy; the two words are separate meanings. A sweet is British for a candy.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull's-eye lantern was a lamp with a bulging lens, and bull's-eyes are also traditional peppermint boiled candies.

clue.text: Name has to be changed? So be it

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding word must be altered in order, giving a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resignedly accepts that their name must be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: The word closing prayers literally means 'so be it', expressing assent or agreement.

clue.text: Draughtsman gets rise in pay

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: pay as a recompense or reward

explanation.surface: A draughtsman is granted a salary increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise in pay' looks like a salary increase, but rise is the upward signal and pay is the word turned. Type double_definition is loose: only Draughtsman defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughtsman is one who draws plans or pictures, literally a drawer.

clue.text: A record about which there's some correspondence?

indicators.note: the following word goes round the preceding phrase, which sits inside it

blocks.note: some, as in 'have you any?'
taken as written
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A disc that has prompted a few letters to the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Correspondence suggests letters about a record; here it means likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogy is a resemblance or parallel between two things, which is one sense of correspondence.

clue.text: Is it similar to a hurricane light?

definitions.text: Is it similar to a hurricane light?

blocks.clueFragment: Is it similar to a hurricane light?
blocks.note: surface reading: a hurricane lamp, a paraffin lantern shielded against wind
setter's reading: a hurricane is a strong blow, so a lamp that works by a jet of blown flame

explanation.walkthrough: A hurricane lamp is a storm lantern; the clue plays on a hurricane being a blow, giving a torch that blasts a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a torch producing a hot directed flame, used for stripping paint or soldering, so it is a lamp driven by a blow.

clue.text: Venerate actor in scene in new production

indicators.note: a new production of a play rearranges it, so the letters are put on afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre review praising a performer's scene in a revival.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate is to make or declare sacred, close to treating something with deep reverence.

clue.text: Area of cricket field used in wet weather

blocks.note: first meaning: the fielding region on the off side, forward of point
second meaning: the tarpaulins dragged over a pitch when it rains

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the covers is a fielding position on the off side; the covers are also sheets protecting the pitch from rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket uses the word both for a fielding zone and for protective sheeting laid over the wicket during rain.

clue.text: Rehearsal for a ventriloquist?

blocks.note: surface reading: a practice attempt before the real thing
setter's reading: a ventriloquist's puppet having a trial outing

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a trial attempt is taken literally as the outing of a ventriloquist's doll.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice or trial attempt before the real event is the standard sense of the phrase.

clue.text: As spectators, observe appearance by cricket side

blocks.note: a look is someone's appearance
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Fans watch a cricket team take the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side, or leg side, is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch without taking part, as onlookers do, is exactly what spectators do.

clue.text: Plot a tailless aircraft

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: an aeroplane

explanation.surface: A scheme involving a flying machine with no tail fin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailless aircraft really exist, so the surface is plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Plot as a noun or verb means a scheme or to scheme, both senses shared.

clue.text: Philanthropist throwing a coin in the water

blocks.note: surface reading: a kindly person who hopes good things for others

blocks.clueFragment: throwing a coin in the water
blocks.note: setter's reading: someone tossing money into a wishing well

explanation.walkthrough: The word for a kind supporter is split literally: one who makes a wish at a wishing well.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wants good fortune for others is benevolent, a loose match for a charitable humanitarian.

clue.text: One who cares is easily hurt

blocks.note: first meaning: one who looks after something, as a bar or a nurse does
second meaning: sore, sensitive

explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes a sensitive carer; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender looks after something, as in bartender, and tender flesh is sore and sensitive to touch.

clue.text: Academic gets important job, but it's drudgery

blocks.note: a university lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge
key means vital, crucial
a task

explanation.surface: A professor lands a senior post that turns out to be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious hard labour, the heavy routine part of a task, is plain drudgery.

clue.text: Clothes holder on a motorbike?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pannier or bag for carrying kit
setter's reading: the metal housing round the cogs of the transmission

explanation.walkthrough: Gear can mean clothing and case a holder, but the real thing is a mechanical housing.
explanation.definitionFit: On machines such as motorcycles, the cogs are enclosed in a protective metal housing named after them.

clue.text: Hero-worship was fatal to him

blocks.note: surface reading: idolising a celebrity
setter's reading: Hero, priestess of Aphrodite in Greek myth, whose lover swam to her nightly

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend a young man swam the Hellespont each night to his beloved Hero and drowned in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical lover who died swimming to Hero is the figure whose devotion killed him.

clue.text: Girl embraces chap up in Hamlet's place

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the girl's name surrounds the other piece
in a down entry, going up means reading the word bottom to top

blocks.note: a girl's name
a man's name

explanation.surface: A girl hugs a man in a village.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like a small village; it is Shakespeare's prince.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish castle where Shakespeare set Hamlet is the prince's home, his place.

clue.text: Express one's views more loudly!

blocks.note: first meaning: voice an opinion openly
second meaning: the call to a quiet speaker to raise the volume

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction; it splits into speaking out and speaking louder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to state an opinion boldly and to talk at greater volume.

clue.text: Pat, due to makeover, is now in fashion

indicators.note: a makeover remodels someone, so the letters are restyled into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thanks to a style overhaul, Pat looks modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Current and modern, abreast of the latest trends, means the same as being fashionable at present.

clue.text: Spaniards accepting article for their wives

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the men's title holds the small word

blocks.note: Spanish gentlemen, by their title
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Spanish men take in a piece of writing on behalf of their spouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their' refers back to the Spaniards, so the definition rests on the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Married Spanish women are addressed by this title, so they are the Spanish gentlemen's spouses.

clue.text: Host of parasites seen on the move

indicators.note: moving about, so the letters change their positions

blocks.note: lice are parasitic insects
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large number of bloodsuckers spotted moving around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host of parasites' suggests an animal carrying lice; host is the landlord. In Britain a pub landlord holds a licence to sell alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensed publican, the landlord who welcomes customers into the pub, acts as their host.

clue.text: Name one dreadfully blase

indicators.note: done dreadfully, so the letters are badly jumbled

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Identify someone who is terribly indifferent.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, the Spanish form of Elizabeth, so an example of a name.

clue.text: You need inspiration to draw one

definitions.text: You need inspiration to draw one

blocks.clueFragment: You need inspiration to draw one
blocks.note: surface reading: an artist needs creative spark to make a picture
setter's reading: inspiration as taking air into the lungs, and draw as inhale

explanation.walkthrough: Inspiration literally means breathing in, and drawing is inhaling, not sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhaling air into the lungs is what you do when you draw this in.

clue.text: Gets beaten, the result of smoking in bed

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
ash is what burning tobacco leaves

explanation.surface: Someone gets a thrashing for smoking in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck hard and violently, battered, is the sense of being bashed.

clue.text: Those having sea views?

blocks.note: surface reading: people owning seaside property
setter's reading: windows that look out over a bay

explanation.walkthrough: 'Those' suggests people, but the things with the views are windows; a bay is also an inlet of sea.
explanation.definitionFit: These are windows projecting outward from a wall, punning on a bay as a coastal inlet.

clue.text: Set of rules the expert may break

blocks.note: first meaning: a body of laws or regulations
second meaning: a cipher that a cryptanalyst cracks

explanation.walkthrough: Breaking rules suggests disobedience; here break means crack, as a cryptanalyst does.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a body of laws, as in the highway code, and also a cipher broken by specialists.

clue.text: Hundreds pocketed by accountants, the rotters!

indicators.note: something pocketed is held inside, so the following word encloses it

blocks.note: CA is chartered accountant; plural CAs
D is the Roman numeral 500, several hundreds

explanation.surface: Accountants pocket hundreds of pounds and are scoundrels.
explanation.walkthrough: Hundreds might suggest C, but the Roman 500 is used. A cad is an old British word for a dishonourable man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is a dated British term for a scoundrel, the same as a dishonourable man.

clue.text: Fear of finishing last by mistake

indicators.note: the finishing part of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: the closing letter of this word
an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone dreads coming last because of a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishing last' reads as coming bottom; finishing picks the end of the word last.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme fear or dread is the plain synonym, as in the reign of fear.

clue.text: Account with date once rendered

indicators.note: rendered means made into something new, so the letters are recast

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bill presented bearing a former date.
explanation.walkthrough: Account and rendered suggest a bill being sent; account is a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A short amusing story about a real incident is a narrative, one kind of account.
